<reason>Side B won by demonstrating that the mandate backfires: it punishes landlords for keeping records (perverse incentive), leads to universal boilerplate disclaimers that provide no information, and creates assumption-of-risk defenses that harm tenants post-signing. While Side A effectively established the information asymmetry problem and asked sharp pressure questions, they failed to neutralize B's argument that the proposed mechanism is counterproductive, particularly the "rolling window" trap that forces permanent boilerplate.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side B's Rebuttal 2 attack on Side A's proposed "rolling window" solution, showing that fraud liability for any subsequent incident would force landlords to use permanent boilerplate disclaimers, rendering the disclosure useless and creating legal defenses against tenants.</best_rebuttal>
